contributorNote: Somali (Af-Soomaali) vocabulary compiled from R. N. Cust (1883), Rev. Fr. Evangelist de Larajasse (1897 "Somali-English and English-Somali Dictionary", Kegan Paul, Trench, Trübner & Co., London — audited 100% line-by-line across Front Matter, Preface pp. v–xiii, Abbreviations p. xiv, 20-row Kenya Reference Table [Swahili sawaheli/sawahili, Ogaden & Darod dialect wa debai, Galla daba galla, East African antelopes si‘g, garanug/lig, adéryo/adéryo ‘ari/godir, b‘e‘id/bi‘‘id, sagaro/sakaro, and rubiad/rubod/rubi currency], and Full Two-Column Page Transcriptions of pp. 26, 123, 127, 242, 266 & 293), Sir Harry H. Johnston (1902), Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1903 "Notes on the Somali Language", 1905 "A Grammar of the Somali Language"), BFBS (1921), Morgan Nilsson (2016), Wendell Kimper et al. (2019), and Anna M. DiGarbo & Rose Stamp (2019). Expanded and cross-verified with Commercially Permissive Datasets (The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0), Google SMOL/GATITOS (en_som, CC-BY-4.0), African Next Voices Maxatire Somali (CC-BY-4.0), DDD Kenyan Somali (CC-BY-4.0), Language Science Press Somali & Marka Corpora (2016/2019, CC-BY-4.0), CLDF Tsammalex & ASJP v20 (CC-BY-4.0), Kaikki.org Somali (CC-BY-SA-4.0)).

entries.english: If we were to go to-morrow, we should catch the man

entries.english: Do you know the difference between a good and a bad man?

entries.english: While he was away on the pilgrimage, his wife had a dream

entries.english: Of the things which are exported from Somaliland, what is the chief?

entries.translation: I don’t want him to go far
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Wahan u malènya, berrí inan tago
entries.translation: I think I am going to-morrow
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.translation: I am waiting for him to come
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.translation: I expect (perhaps) he has run away
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Wahan ù malènya, Burao bu ku tégi
entries.translation: I think he is going to Burao
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Wan ù malén maya in ilach dambi daïso
entries.translation: I don’t think there will be more trouble
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Inla sidàyo ragi wanaksan, la doni maya
entries.translation: (29) one does not want to let good men go
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Àd u garta, wahas wa la húnyihi, o ghainun maha
entries.translation: understand thoroughly that that is very bad and not discipline
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)
Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Wahad ku tiràda, Olesan ghobo, o dochso u tago
entries.translation: tell him to go to Olesan and hurry up
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Nin ú dir, o Ali wahad ku tiràda, sò nocho
entries.translation: send a man to tell Ali to come back
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.translation: I don’t know how to say that
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.translation: if he is here now, call him
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Burao hadian jogo, Garrero ma ímadén
entries.translation: if I had been at Burao, I should not have come to Garrero
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Iminka Burao hadian jogo, laàgti ban ku sin laha
entries.translation: (32) if I were at Burao now, I should give you the money
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.translation: if you had told me before . . .
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Machli maya, hadian u malèyo inu bein shego
entries.translation: I should not listen, if I thought he was telling a lie
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Laag ku sin maya, adigu jogi mahai
entries.translation: I shall not give you pay, if you do not stay
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Haddad jogto, inad egto wad lehda
entries.translation: if you were there, you must have seen
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Hadiad shuchulkà, an donya, anad ghobonin, shuchulkèyga ku ma wanáksanid
entries.translation: (33) if you do not do your work as I want, you are no good to me
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Hukumka machala, amaha humado, amaha sumado
entries.translation: { obey / listen to } the order, whether bad or good
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Hadi hukum lagu shego, wáchaba weidinina
entries.translation: (34) if an order is given you, ask no questions
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Saddehh asho hadiad ka bádsato, laàg heli màysa
entries.translation: (35) if you are more than three days on the road, you will get no pay
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk, Notes on the Somali Language (Oxford University Press, 1903, Vocabulary pp. 42–79) • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Nin walba wa ku húkumyahái, haddu iss yiràdo, wa lagu dúlmya, inu ku so ashtakòdo
entries.translation: (36) every man is allowed, if he imagines he is being ill-treated, to bring a complaint

entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language, Song VIII, p. 178 • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: The misfortune of the other day pains my heart ... Our country is here, though we have been driven to beg (Song XI: Gabei in d, Lament on the Mullah's Raids, 1900–1904)
entries.translation: Da‘wadii doraid ba wadneha i damkineisa e ... Dalkayagi wa kana, haddan laga dawarshaye
entries.pronunciation: da‘wadii doraid ba wadneha i damkineisa e / dalkayagi wa kana
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language, Song XI, pp. 180–181 • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Her colour is like the fruits of Paradise, have you not heard! (Song XII: Gabei in m, My Future Wife)
entries.translation: Midabkèdu wa lèhegyahai midihi jannáda, ma makhásha weiye!
entries.pronunciation: midabkedu wa lehegyahai midihi jannada ma makhasha weiye
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language, Song XII, p. 181 • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: O Dahab, gazelle-eyed! ... Behold how I am! (Song XIII: Gabei in d, To Dahab)
entries.translation: Dahabô, inđo dèralai! ... Sidan ahai daia!
entries.pronunciation: dahabo indho deralai / sidan ahai daia
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language, Song XIII, p. 182 • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: The camels marched in the evening! ... They are the camels of Noble Independence! (Song XIV: Hes in g, Dance Song)
entries.translation: Gèli galabta wa gùrei! ... Wa gèli Gobonimo!
entries.pronunciation: geli galabta wa gurei / wa geli gobonimo
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language, Song XIV, p. 183 • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Traditional birth and marriage tax (1 rupee or 1 ewe ilbir) paid by Somalis to a Yibir (Anas-ki) in exchange for a protective amulet carved from the sacred aldibo tree
entries.translation: samanyo-di / anasnímo-di & awaski aldibo (ghordas-ki / Yibir: godahheđ-ki)
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language, Account of the Yibir and Midgan Dialects pp. 184–185 • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: What men have risen up to seek, may my Lord give thee; my Lord is not stint! (Traditional Yibir blessing chant upon receiving the samanyo gift)
entries.translation: Wihhi rag u kà‘ei, rabbigai ha ku sìyo, rabbigai ma bakhilo!
entries.pronunciation: wihhi rag u ka‘ei rabbigai ha ku siyo rabbigai ma bakhilo
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language, Yibir Blessing Song p. 185 • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Somali tribal protector/patron to whom Midgan (Alowa) hunters attach themselves while hunting with poisoned arrows (wabayo)
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language, Account of the Yibir and Midgan Dialects p. 185 • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Yibir origin myth in which ancestor Mohammed Hanif entered a hill at the challenge of Sultan Au-Bakhardli, winning his descendants the perpetual blood-wit tax of samanyo
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language, Yibir Story pp. 184, 197–199 • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Polysemous Midgan verbal root with 14 derivatives: act/do/fix, catch/hold, accompany, wait, go on, marry, be/exist/live, possess, seek, love, give, and work
entries.translation: raghahh (ku raghahh, la raghahh, so raghahh, si raghahh, raghahho, ku raghahho, raghahhi, raghahhsan, ku raghahhsan, raghahhsano, ku raghahhsano, raghahhsanei, raghahhnin-ki)
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language, Midgan Morphology p. 189 • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Base-5 (quinary) numeral system of the Yibir language (1–10) built on deri ('finger/one') and gànad ('hand/five')
entries.translation: deri (1), limihi (2), sadehhi (3), aferi (4), gànad (5), gànad iyo deri (6), gànad iyo limihi (7), gànad iyo sadehhi (8), gànad iyo aferi (9), limihi gànadod (10)
entries.pronunciation: deri / limihi / sadehhi / aferi / ganad / limihi ganadod
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language, Yibir Numerals pp. 187, 213 • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Higher Yibir numerals (15–1,000) formed by multiples of gànad ('hand = 5') and gođerowi-gi ('rosary = 100')
entries.translation: sadehhi gànadod (15), aferi gànadod (20), gànad gànadod (25), lehh gànadod (30), todoba gànadod (35), sided gànadod (40), sagal gànadod (45), toban gànadod (50), gođerowi-gi (100), tobanihi gođerowiyod (1,000)
entries.pronunciation: sadehhi ganadod / aferi ganadod / godherowi-gi / tobanihi godherowiyod

entries.english: A man who is born a Yibir is not shown the cave (tomb) of Au-Bakhardli (Closing proverb of the Yibir Story of Mohammed Hanif)
entries.translation: Ninki Anas ku đasho, gòdki Au-Bakhardli ma la tuso
entries.pronunciation: ninki anas ku dhasho godki au-bakhardli ma la tuso
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language, Yibir Story p. 199 • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: A Yibir went to Sultan Au-Bakhardli, and asked him for a gift (samanyo) (Opening sentence of the Yibir Story of Mohammed Hanif)
entries.translation: Suldàn Au-Bakhardli ya Anas u tegèđei, o samanyo weidistei
entries.pronunciation: suldan au-bakhardli ya anas u tegedhei o samanyo weidistei
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language, Yibir Story p. 197 • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Are you a Midgan? Yes, I am. Where have you come from? (Midgan identity & greeting exchange)
entries.translation: Alowa ma tahai? Ha, wa ahai. Higged ka so tegèđei?
entries.pronunciation: alowa ma tahai ha wa ahai higged ka so tegedhei
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language, Midgan Sentences #1–3, p. 191 • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Do you understand the Yibir language? Yes, I understand it (Yibir Conversation #5–6)
entries.translation: Khabar Anas ma ku duhúrta? Ha, wa ku duhúra
entries.pronunciation: khabar anas ma ku duhurta ha wa ku duhura
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language, Yibir Conversation p. 196 • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Plural concord contrast: uncontracted fardihi ('the horses', masculine singular verb) vs. contracted fardi ('the horses', feminine singular verb)
entries.translation: Fardihi wa la keinei (masc. sg.) vs. Fardi wa la keinei (fem. sg.)
entries.pronunciation: fardihi wa la keinei vs fardi wa la keinei
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language § 165 Note, p. 91 • Cross-verified with The Thiomi Dataset Somali (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Prefix-conjugated vs. regular suffix-conjugated verb inflection in Somali ('I came, thou camest...' vs. 'I tell, thou tellest...')
entries.translation: wan imi, wad timi, wu yimi, wei timi, weinu nimi vs. wan shega, wad shegta, wu shega, wei shegta, weinu shegna
entries.pronunciation: wan imi wad timi wu yimi wei timi weinu nimi vs wan shega wad shegta wu shega
